page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Surface tension is the force acting per unit
length, perpendicular to an imaginary line drawn
on the surface of a liquid and along the surface.
It arises because surface molecules experience a
net inward attraction from the molecules below.
steps.why: A molecule inside the liquid is attracted equally in all directions; a molecule at the surface has liquid on one side only, so the unbalanced attraction makes the surface behave like a stretched layer measured as force per unit length.
common_mistakes: Saying force per unit area. Per unit area is pressure; surface tension is force per unit LENGTH.
Leaving out perpendicular to the line on the surface.
steps.memory_tip: Tension along a line: force per unit length, not per unit area.
steps.margin_note: The cause sentence (net inward attraction) shows understanding beyond the memorised line.

steps.label: The units
steps.mark_note: the units, written as the boxed line N m⁻¹ — the temperature sentence below it is an unmarked extra

steps.why: Force per unit length is newtons divided by metres, N m⁻¹, and the boxed unit line is what earns this mark. The temperature sentence below it is not part of that mark — it is a one-line extra.
common_mistakes: Writing N m⁻² — that is pressure, one power of length too many.
Writing N m (a product) instead of N per m.
steps.memory_tip: One metre of surface line, so the unit is newton per metre.
steps.margin_note: N m⁻¹ boxed is the marked unit; J m⁻² is the same unit in energy form. The temperature sentence is an unmarked extra, so write the unit first.

insider_note: Per unit length is the tested phrase — per unit area appears in a large share of scripts and loses the definition mark outright.
